sections.description:
PRESIDENT'S ORDER 6 OF 1991
PRESIDENT'S ORDER
6 OF 1991
SUPREME COURT
JUDGES (LEAVE, PENSION AND PRIVILEGES) (SECOND AMENDMENT) ORDER, 1991
[Gazette of
Pakistan, Extraordinary Part I, 1st October, 1991]
No. F.2 (2)/91-Pub., dated
1-10-1991.--The following Order made by the President is hereby published
for general information:---
Whereas it is expedient further
to amend the Supreme Court Judges (Leave, Pension and Privileges) Order, 1968
(P.O. No.1 of 1968), for the purposes hereinafter appearing;
And whereas paragraph 2 of the Fifth
Schedule to the Constitution relating to the Supreme Court provides that every
Judge of the Supreme Court shall be entitled to such privileges and allowances
and to such rights in respect of leave of absence and pension as may be
determined by the President;
Now, Therefore, in exercise of
the powers conferred by the aforesaid paragraph, the President is pleased to
make the following order, namely:--
1. Short title and
commencement.-----(1) This Order may be called the Supreme Court Judges
(Leave, Pension and Privileges) (Amendment) Order, 1991.
(2) It shall come into force with
effect from the 1st day of July, 1991.
2. Amendment of P.O. No. 1 of
1968.----In the Supreme Court Judges (Leave, Pension and Privileges) Order,
1968 (P.O. No. 1 of 1968)----
(a) in paragraph 5, in
sub-paragraph (3), for the word "five" the word "six" shall
be substituted;
(b) after parahraph 7, the
following new paragraph shall be inserted, namely:-
"7-A. Encashment
of leave.---A Judge who has, at the time of retirement, three hundred and
sixty-five days leave on full salary to his credit, shall be paid six months'
salary in lieu of leave not availed of.";
(c) in paragraph 22-A, in
sub-paragraph (2) for the words " two thousand rupees", the words,
"nine thousand rupees" shall be substituted;
(d) in paragraph 22-B, in
sub-paragraph (1), for the words "three hundred" the words "four
hundred" shall be substituted; and
(e) after paragraph 22-C, the
following new paragraph shall be inserted, namely:--
"22-D. Facilities to retired
Judges.--A Judge on retirement shall be entitled at Government expense to
the services of either a driver or an orderly at his option. The services of a
driver or an orderly, as the case may be, will remain available, after the
death of a Judge to his widow. .
